comment: SNOMED CT definition is too narrow. The DPI-H Glossary defines SNOMED CT as "a structured clinical terminology standard for use in electronic health records." This is materially incomplete. SNOMED CT is used for clinical decision support, population health analytics, disease surveillance, research and registry data, AI/ML model training, and interoperability across virtually every digital health domain, not only EHRs. Defining it as an EHR tool understates its architectural relevance to the very components DPI-H describes: the CDSE, HMIS, PHSP, and Terminology Service all depend on SNOMED CT in ways that go beyond EHR coding.

public.suggestedRevision: We suggest a change to the following definition: "SNOMED CT: a comprehensive, multilingual clinical terminology providing a structured, hierarchical representation of clinical concepts including clinical findings, procedures, body structures, and observable entities, used for data capture, clinical decision support, population health analytics, disease surveillance, and research across digital health systems."
